Date: Mon, 27 Nov 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: On-prem queue depth and egress scaling plan

Hi Jared / Nadia —

Thanks again for running the pilot with Nimbus. We want to lock down the sizing assumptions for the private GPU pool (staging -> production transition) and a couple networking constraints that will affect effective throughput: egress caps, burst windows, and per-host queue depth.

Attached is an initial model (nimbus_onprem_capacity_model.xlsx) and an egress map we sketched (egress-map-v1.png). High-level asks:
- Confirm any hard egress caps on the Stargate colo side (sustained vs. burst).
- Verify expected median request size and typical sequence lengths for your RLHF-style rerank flows (helps with token/sec translation).
- Validate whether we should budget for 20–30% additional headroom for cache-warmup/prefetch storms during rollouts.

Our working constraints: total committed GPUs = 16x A100-80GB; target sustained inference throughput = 5,000 req/s (avg payload ~1.2k tokens), 99p latency SLO 250ms for interactive tier. We know these are aggressive; need your input on network egress and host queueing limits so we can tune the batching/queue depth and autoscale thresholds.

Timeline: hoping to finalize the sizing doc and run a staged soak on Wed/Thu this week.

Thanks —
Stephanie
Stephanie Nguyen
Principal Product Manager, Redwood Inference

Date: Mon, 27 Nov 2028 11:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: On-prem queue depth and egress scaling plan

Stephanie — short notes after a first pass through the spreadsheet:

1) Queue depth vs latency tradeoff (quick):
- With 16 GPUs, our runtime sees best utilization when per-GPU inflight requests ~= 12–18 concurrent micro-batches depending on seq length. For the 1.2k token average you called out, start with qdepth 14 and measure CPU->GPU enqueue latencies.
- If egress throttles cause per-request backpressure, queueing will grow and tails will blow past 99p; prefer backpressure signals early (429 or per-route rate limit) rather than silent enqueueing.

2) Autoscale policy suggestion:
- Policy A: target 70% sustained GPU utilization, burst to 90% for up to 10m. If burst >10m, spin +4 GPUs.
- Policy B: for interactive tier, prioritize latency—keep per-GPU qdepth <= 8 and keep 25% spare capacity.

3) Measurement hooks we need from Nimbus:
- per-host egress usage (1m granularity)
- histogram of request payload token counts (p50/p90/p99)

I attached a quick MOP (mop-queueing-scenarios.pdf) with scenario defs.

—Dev
Dev Patel
Senior Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks — quick context from the colo/network side:

- Stargate interconnect enforces per-customer sustained egress caps by default; we can request exceptions but they take 5–7 business days and require an ops readiness letter. Current sustained cap for your rack is 3 Gbps; burst to 12 Gbps for 3 minutes.
- We typically see that short-lived model-rollout storms are the risk: many concurrent small requests (chat) are lighter egress per request than batched rerank workloads, but burstiness still matters.

Practical implications for your spreadsheet:
- Translate token/sec into egress using p95 request size rather than average; spike sizing using p99 will prevent under-provisioning.
- If steady-state needs >3 Gbps sustained we should either: (a) split traffic across two colocations/links, or (b) negotiate a cap increase ahead of the rollout.

I'll pull a week of 1m-aggregated egress for your rack and drop into the shared Drive by EOD.

—Jared
Jared Cole
Infrastructure Lead, Acme Cloud Services

Subject: Re: On-prem queue depth and egress scaling plan

Great context — I reworked the numbers in the XLS and added a short decision matrix. Key changes (summary):

- Two sizing lanes: conservative and aggressive.
  * Conservative: assume sustained egress 3 Gbps (single link). Target sustained req/s = 2,600 (1.2k token avg). Reserve 30% headroom for rollouts -> target pool = 20 GPUs (A100-80GB equiv) with qdepth tuned to 10.
  * Aggressive: assume we get sustained raise or multi-link. Target sustained req/s = 5,200. Reserve 20% headroom -> target pool = 28 GPUs with qdepth tuned to 14 and burst handling rules.

- Network mitigations: split streaming vs. batch egress to separate interfaces where possible; route heavy rerank/embeds through a private link to reduce public egress.

- Instrumentation checklist (for the soak): per-host egress (1m), per-route token histograms, queue-depth gauges, tail-latency traces (p90/p99).

I linked a short test plan in Drive and added comments in the sheet. If we can't get an egress exception, option is to run a traffic-shaping gateway that enforces per-route caps and returns 429 with a Retry-After for non-interactive batch traffic.

Planned soak: Thursday 2028-11-30 02:00–08:00 PST (gradual ramp to conservative sustained load then a 30m aggressive storm).

—Laura
Laura Bennett
Platform Solutions, Redwood Inference

Team — thanks all for quick turn. Final confirmation + next steps: 

1) Soak proceeds as Laura outlined (Thu 11/30 02:00–08:00 PST). Dev will drive runtime-level qdepth experiments during the conservative ramp.
2) Jared: appreciate the egress dump — if the rack shows >2.5 Gbps sustained during the soak we will pause and open a colo exception request. Please upload the historical dump to the Drive link.
3) Vivek: please prepare the autoscale policy PR for both Policy A (utilization-first) and Policy B (latency-first) and include the rollout circuit breaker (max spin every 15m).
4) Nadia: coordinate with Nimbus ops to enable per-host 1m metrics and the token-size histogram; we need these within 24h of the soak start.

Action owners + deadlines placed in the Drive doc. I'll run a quick sync at 23:30 PST tonight to confirm the bump plan. If anything blocks, flag on the thread.

Thanks —
Stephanie
